summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and a history of vascular complications was admitted for left upper extremity pain due to a dialysis graft causing steal syndrome. She underwent successful ligation of the graft and placement of a tunneled hemodialysis catheter in the left internal jugular vein. A CTA showed severe calcification of the radial and ulnar arteries bilaterally, limiting flow assessment, but no central occlusion. Hand surgery recommended outpatient evaluation for possible revascularization. She tolerated dialysis post-procedure, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for vascular and surgical care, along with management of chronic conditions including diabetes, heart failure, and peripheral vascular disease.
